output.title: When definitions drift, fix one workflow first
output.body:
If your team uses the same word three different ways, treat that as a workflow problem first. Not a company-wide theory problem. The practical question is: which single repeating workflow shows signs that the same field, label, or category is being interpreted differently each time?

Pick one process only. In a small business, that might be invoices, customer records, handoffs, or email triage. Then count the rework for two weeks: every time someone has to recategorise something, ask for clarification, fix a duplicate record, or redo an approval because the definition was unclear. Count actual instances, not a vague sense that it is “a lot.”

Once you can see where the drift sits, you can decide whether the next step is a clearer rule, a better template, or a grounded assistant that checks approved definitions in company documents before anything moves forward. That assistant should stay inside company material, not the open web.

If the task needs human judgment, policy sign-off, or context outside the written rule, AI is a helper, not a replacement. And for money movement or other high-risk decisions, the owner still approves it. Customer-owned accounts and code handover are policy, not magic. Start with one workflow, count the drift, then fix the smallest thing that keeps breaking.
